purpose: Input readiness for software architectural design — data model, external interfaces, and UI structure before basic-design generation.

standards.title: ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207:2017
standards.scope: Software architectural design process (§6.4.5) — top-level structure, component identification, interface definition

standards.title: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022
standards.scope: Architecture description — stakeholder concerns, viewpoints, consistency across views

standards.title: ISO/IEC/IEEE 15289:2019
standards.scope: Life-cycle information items — design description (§10.15), database design description (§10.14)

standards.title: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018
standards.scope: Upstream SRS traceability — requirements allocated to design elements (§5.2.8, §9.6.4, §9.6.15)

standards.title: IEEE Std 1016-2009
standards.scope: Software design descriptions — design views/viewpoints; complements 15289 design items

standards.title: ISO/IEC 25010:2011
standards.scope: Quality attributes carried into interface and data design (security, performance, usability)

individualCharacteristics.name: Traceable
individualCharacteristics.check: Every table, endpoint, and screen traces to SRS entities (F-xx, UC-xx, dataEntity)

individualCharacteristics.name: Complete allocation
individualCharacteristics.check: All in-scope SRS requirements are allocated to a BD component (data, API, or screen)

individualCharacteristics.name: Verifiable interfaces
individualCharacteristics.check: API request/response fields and screen form fields are specific enough to test against SRS

individualCharacteristics.name: Consistent views
individualCharacteristics.check: Data model, API contracts, and screen fields are consistent across BD documents

individualCharacteristics.name: No invented scope
individualCharacteristics.check: No endpoints, tables, or screens without graph evidence (UC, feature, or dataEntity backing)

dimensions.label: SRS → design traceability
dimensions.description: Requirements allocated from SRS to BD components with satisfies/tracesTo links

dimensions.label: User interface architecture
dimensions.description: Screens, navigation, actor roles, wireframe structure

dimensions.label: Design constraints
dimensions.description: Technology stack, security, performance limits from SRS NFRs

globalCriteria.question: Confirm the SRS baseline is complete enough to allocate requirements to BD components (no blocking TBD in scope)?
Confirm technology stack, deployment model, and mandated constraints from SRS apply to BD.
Who are the stakeholders for API and UI views (developers, QA, ops, security)? Any viewpoint priorities?
Confirm ID scheme for BD artifacts: API slugs, screen S-xx ids, table names — consistent with graph?
globalCriteria.graphProbe: existing node id patterns in graph

criteria.question: Confirm data entities, relationships, and DBMS constraints from SRS are sufficient for database design.
Confirm retention, classification (PII), and integrity rules per entity are documented in SRS.
criteria.graphProbe: dataEntity nodes with classification or retention

criteria.question: Confirm the API endpoint inventory (method + path + source F-xx/UC-xx) can be derived from the traceability graph.
Confirm default auth model (public, bearer, session, API key) and which endpoints require authentication.
For each endpoint, confirm source F-xx/UC-xx, auth requirements, and request/response fields from graph evidence.
Confirm error response semantics (400/401/403/404/409) per endpoint from UC exception flows.
Confirm the screen inventory (S-xx ids + names + related UC-xx) matches actor-facing use cases in the graph.
Confirm navigation flow between screens (postconditions → target screen) is derivable from UC flows.
For each screen, confirm related UC-xx/F-xx, wireframe components, and bound API endpoints.
Confirm form fields map to API request bodies and table columns map to API response fields.
